title: Scroll Cameras, Circles, Furigana, Frames & Behaviours
description: Five demos of work declared, not scripted: scroll cameras, radial layout, type-level annotation, measuring overlays, composed behaviours.

drops.title: The Camera Is An Attribute
drops.description: Nine camera moves selected by one attribute, each a keyframe set bound to a view timeline instead of a duration.
drops.concept: Dolly is a CSS-only scroll library: you write data-dolly="dolly-in" and the browser does the rest, because every move is a @keyframes rule bound to animation-timeline: view() with an animation-range. This demo isolates that idea — nine moves on one attribute, a range you can retune live, a named view timeline driving a pinned subject, and translateZ depth under a shared perspective. No scroll listener runs on the page.

interaction.mouse: Scroll to drive every move; slide the entry, cover and stagger values to retime them.
interaction.click: Pick one of nine moves for all shots, show the range lines, jump back to the top.
interaction.touch: Scrolling is the whole interface; the panel sits above the reel on small screens.

drops.title: HTML, Arranged on Circles
drops.description: A radial layout system: each child gets an index, the ring turns it into rotate → translate → counter-rotate.
drops.concept: Orbit 2 puts HTML on circles with nothing but custom properties — rings, satellites, reach, range and direction. This demo isolates the placement formula and drives it from container-query units so the reach is measured against the ring's own box, then shows the same ring as a menu, a 270° dial and a universe nested inside one of its own satellites.

interaction.mouse: Slide reach, range, start angle, count and satellite size; hover a satellite to lift it.
interaction.click: Flip direction, keep satellites upright or face them outward, show the lanes.
interaction.touch: All controls are touch-sized; the rings resize with the card.

drops.title: The Reading Is In The Type
drops.description: Plain text in, annotated clusters out — a contextual-substitution pass that writes the ruby nobody typed.
drops.concept: furifont is a Japanese font that carries its own furigana: the reading is part of the glyph, not part of the markup. This demo moves that idea into the browser as a small shaper — longest match wins, a matched run is never re-entered — and applies the same two rules to kanji readings, English IPA and unit tokens, printing the feature code it would have compiled.

interaction.mouse: Tune annotation size, offset and leading; watch clusters highlight.
interaction.click: Turn the feature off to get the plain text back, move annotations below, or limit them to the first occurrence.
interaction.touch: Controls stack under the specimens on small screens.

drops.title: Everything On The Page Is A Layer
drops.description: A design-tool selection frame with handles and live dimensions, painted from a fixed overlay so the page never shifts.
drops.concept: ram wraps text in the selection frame you know from design tools — outline, four corner handles, a live size badge. The point is restraint: the frame must never change the thing it describes. Here every element on a canvas is a target, the overlay is fixed and pointer-events:none, and a ResizeObserver keeps the badge honest while you drag a resizable box.

interaction.mouse: Hover any word, image, button or paragraph to frame it; drag the resizable box's corner.
interaction.click: Click to pin a frame, switch to persistent mode, change handle style, size and colour.
interaction.touch: Tap to pin a frame; persistent mode shows all ten at once.

drops.title: Three Components, Four Behaviours
drops.description: A palette, a multi-select and a menu built from the same popup, selection, typeahead and focus recovery.
drops.concept: Vercel's UI SDK ships behaviours rather than components: you declare a primitive with state and named slots, then attach createPopup, createSelection, createTypeahead or createFocusRecovery to those slots. This demo implements that runtime in vanilla JS and makes the composition visible — detach a behaviour and the widget degrades, taking the ARIA it wrote with it.

interaction.mouse: Open a widget, filter, pick options, watch the inspector log each behaviour.
interaction.click: Toggle any of the four behaviours off and on to re-compose all three components.
interaction.touch: Tap triggers and options; the inspector stacks below on narrow screens.
